paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The Lord's delay is not the Lord forgetting. Scoffers look at a quiet sky and say, "Where is the promise of His coming?" Peter says the Lord "is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance." (2 Peter 3:4, 9)

But patient doesn't mean never, and that matters for how you live today. Peter says the Day of the Lord "will come like a thief," so he asks, "what kind of people ought you to be?" (2 Peter 3:10, 11) His answer is holiness and godliness, with every effort to be found at peace. I know a waiting room is no place to nap, friend, and this is the same. We wait with our ovens hot and our aprons on, and we keep looking forward to "a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells." (2 Peter 3:13)

So how do you stay on your feet while you wait? Peter says to be on guard against the error of the lawless, and to "grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ." (2 Peter 3:17, 18) Every day in the Word is another day of growing, and that's a good use of the Lord's patience. Peter closes with glory to Jesus, and that's where I want my whole life to land too. Amen!
